requirement:
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.

Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` states only observable behavior of the coverage check. It prescribes no library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or named interface.

- "Every function under `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception evidence" is a pass/fail outcome. Suppose the check found unexecuted functions through a different parser, data structure, or pass ordering. It would give the same results and still satisfy the clause. The way functions are found and matched to execution data is therefore discretionary.
- "Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely because their source locations overlap" constrains the attribution result. It does not say how attribution must be built. Span-exclusion, a per-function line ownership map, or any other method that attributes lines correctly would satisfy it.
- "Having no recorded lines alone MUST NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations" restricts which conclusions are valid. It prescribes no mechanism.
- The cited requirements `requirements.test-coverage.check.scope`, `requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions` and `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` give context only. Their own obligations are assessed under their own declarations.

No review roots were supplied. No structural obligation needs implementation evidence, so there is no missing root to report. Test adequacy for these behaviors belongs to the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: Tests adequately cover `requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`.

- Function with no attributable execution needs accepted exception even when its file meets the threshold: `overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent` (file 100% line coverage, `#fn[outer]: zero execution` fails); `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution` (a file exception does not waive `fn a`; a function-level accepted citation passes and is listed under accepted exceptions, including for a not-measured function; a false or fixme review is rejected); `methods_tests_and_helpers_are_included_and_discovery_failures_are_reported` and `default_trait_bodies_and_cfg_exclusions_are_obligations_but_declarations_are_not` (zero-execution/not-measured functions reported; declarations not); the positive case where an executed function passes is in `expanded_async_entries_match_the_fn_keyword_without_borrowing_closure_execution` and in the real flow test `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]`.
- Nested function or closure execution must not cover the enclosing function: `overlapping_nested_functions_and_closures_do_not_cover_the_parent` tests both directions (inner/closure executed but outer not -> outer reported and inner not; outer executed, inner not -> inner reported and outer not); the async test shows closure-only execution leaves `#fn[work]: not measured`; the full-flow test repeats this with real instrumentation (`hidden` reported, `outer` not).
- No recorded lines alone must not establish no obligations: `unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear` (file with `fn missing() {}` and no recorded lines is 'not measured — FAIL' with `#fn[missing]: not measured`; declaration-only file is 'no executable obligations'), plus the `inventory` assertions for macro/derive-only sources in the default-trait test.
- Parse and discovery failures fail the check (covered in the same tests).

No unmarked relevant tests or unassertable obligations were found.

Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.scope
The coverage check MUST consider every explicitly declared function or method
with a body in the first-party Rust sources of
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing`, including test functions,
test helpers, and default trait methods. Declarations without bodies MUST NOT
create execution-coverage obligations. Source discovery or parsing failures
MUST cause the check to fail rather than silently omit functions.
A function whose measurement cannot be established MUST be reported as not
measured rather than silently excluded. Functions excluded by the selected
build configuration require exception evidence under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
